scope: Software-model analysis of the path after _arm_init; not hardware behaviour and not a boot claim

model_state.note: AArch64 high-EL state required, see D-034 third correction

finding_1_model_fidelity_gap.observation: The harness never set boot_args.deviceTreeP, so SecureDTFindEntry could not find /arm-io
finding_1_model_fidelity_gap.consequence: pe_arm_get_soc_base_phys() returns 0 -> pe_identify_machine() returns before bzero/defaults -> gPEClockFrequencyInfo stays BSS zero
finding_1_model_fidelity_gap.verdict: This trap is a model-fidelity gap, not evidence about nuwa: the shipped package does pass the ADT (DarwinBoot.c:630-631 sets Args->DeviceTree/Length)

finding_2_next_blocker_with_adt.observation: Loading the real kernel.macho.adt at a scratch PA and setting deviceTreeP/Length removes the UBSan trap
finding_2_next_blocker_with_adt.explanation: The callee returns the per-CPU base from TPIDR_EL1, which start.s zeroes; the following load therefore dereferences 0xe0
finding_2_next_blocker_with_adt.verdict: Plausible real blocker (a null per-CPU-base dereference), but not proven on hardware: it needs one hardware observation

harness_note: Feeding the ADT is required for any faithful post-arm_init analysis; the pinned crossing test still stops at the arm_init replay point and is unaffected
next_gate: v6: identity VBAR + in-page vectors (catch FAR if it faults) plus markers at _current_percpu_base, _arm_vm_init, _pmap_bootstrap, _kernel_bootstrap
